newsitem.title: PERU: Peru coffee exports double to $162 million.
newsitem.headline: Peru coffee exports double to $162 million.

text.p: Peru's non-decaffeinated coffee exports rose to $162 million in the the first half of the year, up 104 percent compared with the same period in 1996, customs officials said Monday.
Coffee exports in June totaled $93 million, up from $26.2 million during the same time last year, they added.

Peru's coffee-growers have said recent larger-than-usual harvests are due to higher investment in the industry and the presence of the El Nino weather phenomenon, which is forming over the country, bringing higher rainfall to coffee regions.
Peruvian coffee exports are expected to be $320 million this year, compared to $223.1 million in 1996, when Peru exported 90 percent of its coffee, according to industry leaders.
Peru, whose principal coffee harvest is between April and November, is South America's number four producer after Brazil, Colombia and Ecuador, according to the government.
